title: AI bubble burst by...?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if the AI industry experiences an industry downturn by the specified date, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

For the purposes of this market, the AI industry will be considered to have experienced an industry downturn once at least three of the following events have occurred within 90 days of this market's specified timeframe:
- NVIDIA Corporation (NVDA) closing stock price is down 50% from its all-time high.
- iShares PHLX Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) closing stock price is down 40% from its all-time high.
- OpenAI, Inc. or Anthropic PBC declares bankruptcy.
- OpenAI, Inc. is acquired.
- H100 rental price falls to $1.00 or lower for five consecutive days, as shown on the SiliconData Silicon Index at:
https://www.silicondata.com/products/silicon-index.
- Major AI Hardware Supplier Collapse: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited (TSM), ASML Holding N.V. (ASML), Broadcom Inc. (AVGO), Arista Networks, Inc. (ANET), or Super Micro Computer, Inc. (SMCI), closing stock price is down 50% from its all-time high.

This market may resolve immediately once three conditions have been met within 90 days of the specified timeframe.

This market will not resolve to "Yes" until three conditions have been met, regardless of reporting of an industry downturn or similar claims.

The primary resolution source will be official information from the respective companies and listing exchanges; however, a consensus of credible reporting will also be used.

eventMetadata.context_description: Heavy capital expenditures by hyperscalers and AI labs continue to outpace monetization of large language models and agentic systems, sustaining trader caution on an imminent bubble burst despite competitive model releases. OpenAI's roughly $13 billion 2025 revenue against multi-year losses, paired with Google's May 2026 Gemini 3.5 and Gemini Omni launches at I/O, underscore the gap between capability demonstrations and profitable scaling. The July 2026 implosion of the AI-focused Situational Awareness hedge fund after leveraged bets failed amplified concerns over circular funding among chipmakers, cloud providers, and developers. Key near-term catalysts include Nvidia and Micron earnings plus potential OpenAI or Anthropic IPO timelines, which could clarify returns or expose financing pressures in a market assigning only modest implied probability to a 2026 burst.
